title: Painting the religious heart of Haarlem
description: A quick jaunt from Amsterdam, the old town of Haarlem spills out from a lovely square with Saint Bavo Church at its center. This Smarthistory video explains Pieter Saenredamthe’s meticulous 1631 painting of the church during the town’s cultural heyday.

title: Gauguin casts himself as an outlaw in a portrait for Van Gogh
description: Gauguin painted it in Brittany in 1888 and sent it to Vincent van Gogh in an exchange of portraits. It is in the Van Gogh Museum on Museumplein.

title: Van Gogh’s search for authenticity
description: This video from Smarthistory analyzes The Potato Eaters, a memorable canvas at the Van Gogh Museum. The art historians explain Van Gogh’s penchant for painting peasants and how his rough brush strokes evoke the hardscrabble life of the family pictured.

title: Silver, porcelain and a peeled lemon glow in the dark
description: Kalf painted luxury objects from Dutch trade, including Chinese porcelain, around 1655–60. It is in the Rijksmuseum, the national museum on Museumplein.

title: Athens builds a marble temple to announce its golden age
description: Two art historians look closely at the temple on the Acropolis rock that Iktinos and Kallikrates built for Athena between 447 and 432 BCE, with sculpture directed by Phidias, and at what Periclean Athens meant it to say about itself.

title: Six marble women hold up a temple roof on their heads
description: Two art historians look at one of the caryatids from the south porch of the Erechtheion, the temple on the Acropolis built in 421–407 BCE, and at how a column could be turned into a standing woman without looking like it was carrying a load.

title: A marble youth shifts his weight and sculpture comes alive
description: The Kritios Boy, carved around 480 BCE and found buried in the debris the Persians left on the Acropolis, is now in the Acropolis Museum. Its relaxed stance, weight on one leg, marks the break from stiff Archaic figures.

title: A smiling marble maiden still carries traces of her paint
description: The Peplos Kore, a votive statue of a young woman from about 530 BCE, stood on the Acropolis until the Persian sack. Now in the Acropolis Museum’s Archaic gallery, she shows how brightly painted Greek sculpture once was.

title: A pot as tall as a man marks an aristocrat’s grave
description: Around 750 BCE this huge amphora stood over a woman’s grave in the Dipylon cemetery at Kerameikos, the potters’ quarter by the city gate. Its bands of meander pattern frame one of the earliest scenes of mourners in Greek art.

title: Citizens vote with pottery shards in a crowded marketplace
description: The Ancient Agora below the Acropolis was where Athenians shopped, argued, held trials and ran their democracy. The film looks at its law courts, council house and stoas; finds such as ostraka are shown in the rebuilt Stoa of Attalos.

title: A fallen soldier’s statue asks passers-by to stop and mourn
description: This kouros, about 530 BCE, marked the grave of a young man named Kroisos in the Attic countryside; its base asks viewers to pause for one killed in battle. It is now a centrepiece of the National Archaeological Museum’s Archaic rooms.

title: A bronze god poised to throw, recovered from the seabed
description: The Artemision Bronze, cast around 460 BCE and pulled from a shipwreck off Cape Artemision in 1926–28, stands in the National Archaeological Museum. Scholars still argue whether his missing weapon was Zeus’s thunderbolt or Poseidon’s trident.

title: A woman picks a necklace from her jewellery box, forever
description: Hegeso’s grave relief, carved around 410 BCE, stood along the Street of Tombs in the Kerameikos cemetery, where a cast now marks its place. The original, showing her seated with a servant, is in the National Archaeological Museum.

title: A shipwreck preserves a bronze youth that melting would have destroyed
description: Most ancient bronzes were melted down for metal; this life-size youth from about 340 BCE survived because the ship carrying it sank. Sponge divers raised it in 1900, and it now stands in the National Archaeological Museum.

title: An odd-shaped temple squeezes several cults onto sacred ground
description: The Erechtheion on the Acropolis, built in the late 400s BCE beside the Parthenon, sits on uneven rock and shelters older shrines, including the spot of Athena’s sacred olive tree. Its four sides and different levels follow from that.

title: A goddess bends to fix her sandal in rippling drapery
description: A relief of about 410 BCE from the parapet around the Temple of Athena Nike on the Acropolis, carved in clinging, wet-looking folds. It is in the Acropolis Museum below the hill.

title: Two museums argue over the marbles of one temple
description: Greece has asked for decades for the sculptures Lord Elgin removed around 1801. The Acropolis Museum, opened in 2009 below the Acropolis, keeps space for the frieze it hopes to reunite.

title: A gold death mask named for a king who probably wasn’t
description: Heinrich Schliemann found the gold mask in a shaft grave at Mycenae in 1876; it predates the Trojan War era by centuries. It is in the National Archaeological Museum on Patission Street.

title: Gaudí’s church reads like a Bible carved in stone
description: Two art historians walk around the basilica and read its façades: the Nativity side Gaudí lived to see built, the stark Passion side added after his death, and the forest of tree-like columns that holds up the nave without flying buttresses.

title: A painting that broke modern art is named for a Barcelona street
description: Picasso’s 1907 canvas of five women takes its title from Carrer d’Avinyó, a narrow street in the Gothic Quarter he knew as a teenager in Barcelona. Smarthistory explains how its masks and splintered space opened the road to Cubism.

title: A stiff wooden Madonna holds the Christ child on her lap
description: A painted Romanesque wood carving from the 12th century, from the village of Ger in the Cerdanya. It is in the Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya, in the Palau Nacional on Montjuïc.

title: Romanesque stone capitals carved with tiny stories
description: Carved capitals from the church of Sant Miquel in Camarasa in the Noguera, Lleida province. They are in the Romanesque galleries of the Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya on Montjuïc.

title: Five girls with lit lamps, five shut out in the dark
description: Wall paintings of around 1100 from a side apse of a small church at Pedret, near Berga; they were removed in 1921. They are in the Museu Nacional d’Art de Catalunya in the Palau Nacional on Montjuïc.

title: The stunning statue of Nefertiti
description: The dramatic presentation in the Neues Museum of the iconic bust of Nefertiti makes for an exceptional museumgoing experience. This video from Smarthistory expertly explains details about the sculpture itself and Nefertiti’s influential role in Egypt.

title: The incredible Ishtar Gate
description: The Ishtar Gate at the Pergamon Museum is among the most awe-inspiring artifacts in any museum in Europe. In this video from Smarthistory, two art historians passionately describe the gate and its role as the entrance to the fortified city of Babylon.

title: A tiny wooden queen with a stern face and heavy lids
description: A small yew-wood head of Queen Tiye, mother of Akhenaten, from around 1355 BCE; later reworked with a wig and feathered crown. It is in the Egyptian Museum in the Neues Museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: Gods and giants wrestle across a marble staircase
description: The Hellenistic altar from Pergamon in Asia Minor, about 170 BCE, with its long frieze of the gods’ battle against the giants. It was rebuilt inside the Pergamonmuseum on Berlin’s Museum Island, now closed for renovation.

title: A pharaoh kisses his child under the rays of the sun
description: A limestone house altar from Amarna, around 1350 BCE, showing the royal family at ease beneath the sun-disc Aten. It is in the Egyptian Museum in the Neues Museum on Berlin’s Museum Island, near the bust of Nefertiti.

title: A Haarlem tavern woman laughs with an owl on her shoulder
description: Hals’s portrait of “Mad Babbe”, a real Haarlem woman of the 1630s, painted in loose, fast strokes with a tankard and an owl. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: A boy beats time with his hand, caught mid-song
description: Hals painted this half-length boy around 1623–25 with quick, visible brushstrokes, possibly as a picture of the sense of hearing. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: A centaur raises a rock over a tiger in tiny stone tiles
description: A Roman floor mosaic from around 130 CE, found at the emperor Hadrian’s villa at Tivoli, with a centaur defending his mate from big cats. It is in the Antikensammlung at the Altes Museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: A whole village acts out more than a hundred sayings
description: Bruegel’s 1559 panel turns Dutch proverbs into people banging heads against walls and casting roses before swine. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: A man waits for a young woman to finish her glass
description: Vermeer’s interior from around 1660, with a stained-glass window, a lute on a chair and a quiet courtship. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: A giant Virgin stands in a Gothic church full of light
description: A small panel from around 1440 in which Mary is taller than the nave around her and sunlight falls through the windows. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: An empty Renaissance city waits for people who never arrive
description: A long painted panel from the 1490s, attributed to Francesco di Giorgio Martini, showing an ideal city of colonnades and palaces in perfect perspective. It is in the Gemäldegalerie at Berlin’s Kulturforum.

title: Three kings bring gifts in rich robes to a ruined stable
description: The central panel of an altarpiece from around 1470, named after the Spanish monastery at Monforte where it stood until 1914. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: Angels and apostles crowd around Mary’s body on a gold ground
description: A Florentine panel from around 1310 by Giotto and his workshop, showing the Virgin laid in her tomb as Christ receives her soul. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: A German merchant in London poses among his letters and seals
description: Holbein’s 1532 portrait of a Hanseatic trader at the Steelyard in London, surrounded by scales, coins and a glass vase of carnations. It is in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin’s old master gallery at the Kulturforum.

title: A married couple sit side by side and do not quite connect
description: Manet’s 1879 painting of a fashionable couple among potted plants, bought by the Berlin museum in 1896. It hangs in the Alte Nationalgalerie, the 19th-century art museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: Friedrich’s wife looks out at masts on the river from his studio
description: An 1822 painting of the artist’s wife Caroline at the window of his Dresden studio above the Elbe, seen from behind. It hangs in the Alte Nationalgalerie, the 19th-century art museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: A painter pauses to listen as a skeleton plays at his shoulder
description: Böcklin’s 1872 self-portrait, with Death bowing a single string just behind him. It hangs in the Alte Nationalgalerie, the 19th-century art museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: A single battered oak stands over a wide green plain
description: Friedrich’s 1822 landscape of a shepherd resting under an old oak with distant mountains behind. It hangs in the Alte Nationalgalerie, the 19th-century art museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: Monks carry a coffin into a ruined abbey in the snow
description: Friedrich painted this winter funeral among bare oaks in 1809–10 as a pair with Monk by the Sea. It hangs in the Alte Nationalgalerie, the 19th-century art museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: A tiny figure stands before a huge dark sea and sky
description: Friedrich’s 1808–10 painting puzzled its first viewers with its almost empty composition; the Prussian crown prince bought it. It hangs in the Alte Nationalgalerie, the 19th-century art museum on Berlin’s Museum Island.

title: A Dada collage slices up Weimar Germany’s politicians
description: Höch’s 1919–20 photomontage of cut-up magazine pictures, mixing generals, Dada artists and machines; it was shown at the 1920 Dada Fair. It belongs to Berlin’s Nationalgalerie, shown at the Neue Nationalgalerie at the Kulturforum.

title: A murdered revolutionary is painted like a martyred saint
place: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
description: Two art historians look closely at Jacques-Louis David’s 1793 painting of Jean-Paul Marat, stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday. The canvas hangs in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, on Rue de la Régence.

title: Gold collars and discs show Bronze Age Ireland’s wealth
description: Ireland had rich gold sources in the Bronze Age, and smiths beat it into crescent collars, discs and torcs. The best of them are in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: Two boys digging potatoes find Ireland’s finest chalice
description: Found in 1868 by two boys digging potatoes in a ringfort in County Limerick, the eighth-century Ardagh Chalice combines silver, gold filigree and enamel. It sits in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: A plain iron bell gets a jewelled case eight centuries later
description: The iron bell is said to have belonged to Saint Patrick; its bronze and gold shrine was made around 1100. Both are in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: A processional cross made to hold a fragment of the True Cross
description: Made around 1123 for Turlough O’Connor, High King of Ireland, and kept for centuries at Cong in County Mayo. It is in the National Museum of Ireland’s archaeology building on Kildare Street.

title: Monks fill a gospel book with spirals, beasts and tiny jokes
place: Book of Kells, Old Library, Trinity College
description: An illuminated gospel book made around 800, probably begun on the island of Iona and finished at Kells. It is kept in the Old Library at Trinity College Dublin, where a few pages are shown at a time.

title: A Gauguin of praying Breton women ends up in Edinburgh
description: Gauguin painted this Breton scene in 1888 at Pont-Aven, with a flat red field and the women’s vision of Jacob wrestling an angel. The Scottish National Gallery on the Mound bought it in 1925; this conversation unpacks its break with Impressionism.

title: A flat church wall opens into a painted chapel
description: Masaccio’s fresco in Santa Maria Novella church, painted around 1427, is one of the first uses of single-point perspective. Below the Trinity, a skeleton on a tomb carries a warning to the living. Two art historians explain how it works.

title: Bronze doors take a goldsmith 27 years to finish
description: Lorenzo Ghiberti cast ten gilded Old Testament panels for the east doors of the Baptistery, facing the cathedral. Michelangelo is said to have named them. The originals are now indoors in the cathedral museum; copies hang on the building.

title: A friar paints the Annunciation at the top of the stairs
description: Fra Angelico was a Dominican friar at San Marco convent, and he painted this fresco where his brothers would see it each time they climbed to their cells. It is quiet, spare and meant for prayer. The convent is now a museum.

title: A young painter gives the apostles real weight and shadow
place: Brancacci Chapel, Santa Maria del Carmine
description: In the Brancacci Chapel of Santa Maria del Carmine church, Masaccio painted figures lit from a single direction and standing on solid ground. His weeping Adam and Eve, driven out of Eden, became a school for later artists, Michelangelo among them.

title: Michelangelo carves Night and Day for two Medici tombs
description: The New Sacristy behind San Lorenzo church is a room Michelangelo designed both as architecture and as a setting for his sculpture. Reclining figures of Night, Day, Dawn and Dusk lie on the tombs of two minor Medici dukes.

title: A library staircase spills down into its own lobby
description: Michelangelo designed the Medici family’s library above the cloister of San Lorenzo church. Its tall, cramped vestibule breaks classical rules on purpose, and the staircase seems to pour out of the reading room like a slow flow of stone.

title: A boy hero in bronze stands nude for the first time in centuries
description: Donatello’s bronze David, probably made for the Medici palace courtyard, was the first freestanding male nude since antiquity. It now stands in the Bargello, the former police headquarters and prison that houses the city’s sculpture museum.

title: Four stonemasons die rather than carve a pagan god
description: The stonemasons’ and woodworkers’ guild picked four Christian sculptors martyred for refusing to make a statue for the Roman emperor. Nanni di Banco carved them as a group of Roman-looking men in conversation for their niche on Orsanmichele church.

title: The armorers’ guild orders a saint in shining marble armor
description: Each guild filled a niche on the outside of Orsanmichele, a grain hall turned church. The armorers chose St George and hired Donatello. The marble original moved to the Bargello museum; a copy stands in the niche on Via dell’Arte della Lana.

title: A goldsmith raises the largest dome of its age with no wooden frame
description: The cathedral sat with a hole in its roof for decades because no one knew how to span it. Brunelleschi built the dome without wooden centering, using two shells, herringbone brickwork and hoisting machines of his own design, finishing in 1436.

title: A painted panel and a mirror teach artists to draw in depth
place: Duomo central doorway, facing the Baptistery
description: Around 1420 Brunelleschi stood inside the cathedral doorway and painted the Baptistery opposite, then had viewers compare it with the real building through a hole and a mirror. The demonstration gave painters a working system of linear perspective.

title: An angel kneels and Mary half turns away in gilded stone
description: Donatello made this gilded sandstone relief in the 1430s for the Cavalcanti family. It is still set into the right wall of the nave in Santa Croce, the Franciscan basilica on the east side of the centre.

title: Verrocchio’s David is a skinny teenager who has just won
description: A bronze David made for the Medici around 1470, wiry and pleased with himself, with Goliath’s head at his feet. It stands in the Bargello, the former police headquarters and prison that is now the sculpture museum.

title: Florence’s first bronze doors tell the Baptist’s story in 28 panels
description: Andrea Pisano finished the doors in 1336, the earliest of the Baptistery’s three sets. The originals are now in the Museo dell’Opera del Duomo, with copies in the frames on the Baptistery across the square.

title: The linen weavers’ saint stands firmly on a cushion of cloth
description: Donatello carved this marble figure around 1411–13 for the linen weavers’ niche on Orsanmichele, the guild church. The original is in the museum upstairs at Orsanmichele, with a copy outside.

title: Donatello carves a penitent saint worn down to skin and bone
description: A painted wooden figure from the 1450s showing the Magdalene as a hermit in the desert, gaunt and covered by her own hair. It is in the Museo dell’Opera del Duomo, the cathedral museum behind the Duomo.

title: Michelangelo’s giant keeps watch for the young republic
description: Carved from a block other sculptors had given up on, it stood outside the town hall from 1504 as a symbol of the republic. The original moved indoors in 1873 to the Galleria dell’Accademia on Via Ricasoli.

title: Venus presides over a spring garden full of flowers
description: Painted around 1480 for the Medici, with Venus, Mercury, the Three Graces and Flora in an orange grove. It hangs in the Uffizi, the old Medici office building that became one of Europe’s first public galleries.

title: Two goldsmiths compete for the Baptistery’s bronze doors
description: In 1401 the cloth merchants’ guild asked artists for a trial panel of the sacrifice of Isaac. Ghiberti’s won and Brunelleschi’s lost, and both now hang side by side in the Bargello, the city’s sculpture museum.

title: Pastel figures carry Christ’s body with no ground to stand on
description: An altarpiece from the 1520s in bright pinks and blues, with no cross, tomb or landscape to anchor the scene. It is still in the Capponi Chapel of Santa Felicita, a small church just south of the Ponte Vecchio.

title: A banker’s house sets the pattern for Renaissance palaces
description: Michelozzo built it for Cosimo de’ Medici from 1444, with rough stone below and smoother floors above. The family lived here for about a century. It stands on Via Cavour and is now Palazzo Medici Riccardi.

title: A Flemish altarpiece arrives and Florentine painters take notes
description: A Medici banker in Bruges ordered this huge Nativity in the 1470s and shipped it to Florence, where its rough shepherds and fine detail impressed local painters. It is now in the Uffizi, the city’s main picture gallery.

title: Cimabue sets the Virgin on a throne above four prophets
description: A tall altarpiece from around 1290 made for the church of Santa Trinita, with Hebrew prophets in arches beneath the throne. It hangs in the Uffizi, the city’s main picture gallery, next to Duccio’s and Giotto’s Madonnas.

title: A giant Bible copied in England was meant as a gift for the pope
description: The oldest complete Latin Bible, made by monks at Wearmouth-Jarrow in northeast England around 700, and weighing about 34 kilos. It belongs to the Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, the Medici library at San Lorenzo.

title: A towering Madonna long credited to Cimabue turns out to be Duccio’s
description: The Sienese painter Duccio made this Virgin and Child in 1285 for a confraternity at Santa Maria Novella. It hangs in the Uffizi, the city’s main picture gallery, beside the big Madonnas of Cimabue and Giotto.

title: Gold and flowing lines frame an angel’s greeting, Siena style
description: Painted in 1333 for Siena cathedral, with the angel’s words raised in gold and Mary drawing back. It was brought to Florence in the 18th century and hangs in the Uffizi, the city’s main picture gallery.

title: Giotto’s Virgin sits solidly on her throne, with real weight
description: Painted around 1310 for the church of Ognissanti, it shows Mary as a heavy, rounded figure in a Gothic throne. It hangs in the Uffizi, the city’s main picture gallery, beside Cimabue’s and Duccio’s Madonnas.

title: Venus drifts ashore on a scallop shell
description: Botticelli painted it on canvas in the 1480s, a large mythological nude rare for its time. It hangs in the Uffizi Gallery, the Medici office building beside Piazza della Signoria.

title: Two women hold down a general and cut off his head
description: Artemisia painted this version around 1620 for Cosimo II de’ Medici. It hangs in the Uffizi Gallery, the Medici office building beside Piazza della Signoria.

title: The Magi arrive with a glittering retinue of horses and hounds
description: Painted in 1423 for Palla Strozzi, Florence’s richest man, with real gold and raised patterns throughout. It hangs in the Uffizi Gallery, beside Piazza della Signoria.

title: Alberti gives a Gothic church a classical front
description: Commissioned by the Rucellai family in 1456, the green and white marble façade adds scrolls and a temple pediment to a medieval base. It faces Piazza Santa Maria Novella near the station.

title: Fruit, a bird’s nest and insects on a forest floor
description: Ruysch, court painter to the Elector Palatine, painted it in 1711; her still lifes sold for more than Rembrandt’s did. It is in the Uffizi Gallery, beside Piazza della Signoria.

title: Adam hides his face and Eve howls as they leave Eden
place: Brancacci Chapel, Santa Maria del Carmine
description: Masaccio’s fresco of around 1425, one of the most emotional figures of the early Renaissance; fig leaves added later were removed in the 1980s. It is in the Brancacci Chapel in Santa Maria del Carmine, Oltrarno.

title: Perseus holds up Medusa’s head over the city’s main square
place: Loggia dei Lanzi, Piazza della Signoria
description: Cellini cast the bronze for Cosimo I de’ Medici and unveiled it in 1554, after a dramatic pour he wrote about in his memoirs. It stands in the Loggia dei Lanzi on Piazza della Signoria.

title: A merchant’s palace wears the three classical orders
description: Designed by Alberti for Giovanni Rucellai around 1450, its façade layers pilasters storey by storey over smooth rusticated stone. It is on Via della Vigna Nuova.

title: Two towering Madonnas show painting turn toward real bodies
description: Cimabue’s altarpiece of about 1280 and Giotto’s of about 1310 hang in the same room, so the shift in weight and space is easy to compare. They are in the Uffizi Gallery, beside Piazza della Signoria.

title: A cube topped by a dome makes one of the first Renaissance rooms
description: Brunelleschi’s sacristy of the 1420s was built for the Medici, with roundels by Donatello. It is in the basilica of San Lorenzo, the Medici parish church near the central market.

title: A church built from rows of identical arches and chapels
description: Brunelleschi designed this Augustinian church in the 1430s on a strict grid of grey stone and white plaster; it was finished after his death. It faces Piazza Santo Spirito in the Oltrarno district.

title: A duchess in a brocade gown sits with her young son
description: Bronzino’s 1545 portrait of the wife of Cosimo I de’ Medici, her brocade gown painted thread by thread. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery beside the Palazzo Vecchio.

title: A grinning angel lifts the baby Jesus toward his mother
description: Lippi’s painting from around 1460–65, with a landscape seen through a window behind the young Madonna. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery beside the Palazzo Vecchio.

title: A Sienese painter builds a deep temple behind the figures
description: Lorenzetti’s 1342 altarpiece for Siena Cathedral, set inside a painted church with a gilded dome. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery beside the Palazzo Vecchio.

title: Pastel saints stand in a sunlit loggia with the Virgin
description: Domenico Veneziano painted this around 1445–47 for Santa Lucia dei Magnoli, with a painted courtyard of coloured marble. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery beside the Palazzo Vecchio.

title: A nude Venus looks straight out while maids search a chest
description: Titian’s 1538 painting for Guidobaldo della Rovere, later Duke of Urbino, inspired Manet’s Olympia. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery beside the Palazzo Vecchio.

title: An elegant Madonna stretches like a swan
description: Parmigianino worked on this altarpiece from 1534 until his death and left it unfinished, with a single column in the background. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery beside the Palazzo Vecchio.

title: Two children play with a small bird in a field
description: Raphael painted this around 1505–06 as a wedding gift; it broke into pieces in a 1547 house collapse and was repaired. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery beside the Palazzo Vecchio.

title: A duke and duchess face each other in strict profile
description: Piero’s double portrait of the rulers of Urbino, with their triumphs on the back; the duke is shown from his left after losing his right eye. It is in the Uffizi, Florence’s great picture gallery.

title: Mars breaks free from Venus while Europe mourns
description: Rubens painted this allegory of the Thirty Years’ War in 1637–38 and explained it in a letter. It hangs in the Palatine Gallery of Palazzo Pitti, the Medici palace on the Oltrarno.

title: Small hexagons show people inventing farming and weaving
description: Reliefs by Andrea Pisano and his workshop from the 1330s for Giotto’s bell tower, showing human labour and the arts. The originals are in the Museo dell’Opera del Duomo, with copies on the tower.

title: Byzantine mosaics turn a small monastery church into a vision of heaven
description: The Chora, a monastery church near the Edirnekapı land walls, was redecorated around 1320 by the statesman Theodore Metochites. Its gold mosaics and the fresco of Christ pulling Adam and Eve from their tombs are among the finest late Byzantine art.

title: Sinan crowns a hilltop with a sultan’s mosque and its little city
description: The architect Mimar Sinan finished this mosque for Süleyman the Magnificent in 1558 on the Third Hill above the Golden Horn. Around it he built schools, a hospital, a soup kitchen and baths, and the tombs of Süleyman and his wife Hürrem lie in the garden.

title: A grand vizier hides a jewel box of Iznik tiles above the market
description: Rüstem Pasha, Süleyman’s grand vizier and son-in-law, had Sinan raise this small mosque on a platform over rented shops near the Spice Bazaar. Inside, almost every surface is covered in Iznik tiles, including the new tomato-red glaze of the 1560s.

title: Justinian’s smaller domed church tries out ideas for Hagia Sophia
description: Built in the 520s and turned into a mosque around 1500, its octagonal plan under a dome anticipates Hagia Sophia. It is known as Little Hagia Sophia and stands near the Sea of Marmara shore below Sultanahmet.

title: Sinan’s first great mosque mourns a sultan’s favourite son
description: Süleyman the Magnificent ordered this mosque in 1543 after his son Mehmed died young, and it was Sinan’s first major imperial commission. It stands in the Şehzadebaşı district near the Valens Aqueduct.

title: The first mosaic after Iconoclasm shows Mary on a gold throne
description: Unveiled in 867, the enthroned Virgin and Child marked the return of religious images after the Iconoclast period. It sits high in the apse of Hagia Sophia in Sultanahmet.

title: A sixth-century dome seems to float on a ring of light
description: Justinian’s builders raised Hagia Sophia in under six years after riots burned its predecessor in 532. Art historians show how forty windows at the base of the dome make it look weightless, and how the church shaped Byzantine and Ottoman architecture.

title: A museum for 86 years turns back into a working mosque
description: Hagia Sophia was a church for nine centuries, a mosque for nearly five, a museum from 1934, and a mosque again from 2020. Two Byzantine art historians look at what the minarets, mihrab and great calligraphic roundels added to the building.

title: Mary and John plead with Christ in fine glass tesserae
description: A thirteenth-century mosaic, damaged in its lower half, with soft modelling in tiny glass cubes. It is in the upper south gallery of Hagia Sophia in Sultanahmet.

title: Alexander the Great charges into battle on a king’s coffin
description: A marble sarcophagus of the late fourth century BCE from the royal necropolis of Sidon, still with traces of paint. It is in the Istanbul Archaeology Museums, beside Topkapı Palace.

title: A blindfolded teenage queen gropes for the executioner’s block
description: Delaroche’s 1833 painting of the nine-day queen’s death in 1554 was thought destroyed in a 1928 flood until it turned up rolled in storage. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A merchant couple, a dog and a tiny mirror reflecting the room
description: Van Eyck’s 1434 portrait of a Bruges merchant and his wife, signed on the wall above the convex mirror. Two art historians look closely at it in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Two blue and white vases carry a date: 1351
description: A pair of Chinese porcelain temple vases whose inscription dates them precisely, making them key to the history of blue-and-white ware. They are in the British Museum’s Chinese galleries in Bloomsbury.

title: A couple in a theatre box look anywhere but the stage
description: Renoir showed this 1874 picture of a fashionable woman and her opera-glass-wielding companion at the first Impressionist exhibition. It belongs to the Courtauld Gallery in Somerset House on the Strand.

title: An Assyrian king records an Israelite ruler bowing at his feet
description: A black limestone monument from Nimrud, about 825 BCE, listing the campaigns of Shalmaneser III. One panel shows King Jehu of Israel kneeling with tribute. It stands in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: Shell collectors on a Kent beach miss a comet overhead
description: Dyce painted his family gathering shells under ancient chalk cliffs, with Donati’s comet faint in the evening sky. The painting is in Tate Britain, the national gallery of British art on Millbank.

title: Hamlet’s drowned heroine floats among carefully painted flowers
description: Millais painted the riverbank outdoors in Surrey and the figure in his studio, with model Elizabeth Siddal lying in a bath. The 1852 painting is one of the best-known works in Tate Britain on Millbank.

title: An earl builds himself a Roman villa beside the Thames
description: Lord Burlington designed this Palladian villa in the 1720s as a place for art, books and entertaining rather than living. The house and its gardens are open to visitors in Chiswick, west London.

title: A gold and enamel Last Judgement built around one thorn
description: Made around 1400 for Jean, Duke of Berry, to hold a thorn said to come from Christ’s crown. It came to the museum in the Waddesdon Bequest and is on show in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: A Sumerian box shows chariots on one side and a banquet on the other
description: A small wooden box inlaid with shell, red limestone and lapis lazuli, found in a royal grave at Ur in Iraq and dating to about 2500 BCE. It is in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: A swing, a slipper flying off, and a hidden admirer
description: A small Rococo painting from around 1767 of a young woman on a swing above a man in the bushes. Fragonard took the job after another painter refused. It hangs in the Wallace Collection, Hertford House on Manchester Square.

title: One stone with three scripts unlocks Egyptian hieroglyphs
description: A priests’ decree from 196 BCE written in hieroglyphs, demotic and Greek, found by French soldiers in 1799 and taken by the British in 1801. It is in the British Museum in Bloomsbury, in the Egyptian sculpture gallery.

title: Northumbrian monks paint a gospel book in knots and birds
description: A gospel book made on Holy Island around 700, credited to Bishop Eadfrith, with a later Old English translation squeezed between the lines. It is kept at the British Library on Euston Road, next to St Pancras station.

title: An archangel in ivory looks like a classical god
description: A large ivory panel from around 525, likely made in Constantinople, showing Michael holding an orb and staff at the top of a flight of steps. It is in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: A king’s ship grave holds gold from across two continents
description: Dug from an East Anglian field in 1939, the seventh-century ship burial held a helmet, gold buckle and silver from as far as Byzantium. The finds are in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: A pagan priestess offers incense as Rome turns Christian
description: An ivory leaf carved around 400 CE for a Roman family that kept faith with the old gods, showing a priestess at an altar. It is in the V&A, the South Kensington museum of art and design.

title: Stone fans hang from the ceiling of a Tudor king’s chapel
place: Henry VII Lady Chapel, Westminster Abbey
description: Henry VII built this Lady Chapel from 1503 as his own burial place, under a fan-vaulted ceiling with stone pendants. It sits at the east end of Westminster Abbey, where monarchs are crowned.

title: A peacock and a cucumber crowd into an angel’s visit
description: Crivelli painted this Annunciation in 1486 for a church in Ascoli Piceno, packing a busy town street with carpets, birds and fruit. It hangs in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A farm cart fords a Suffolk stream on a summer afternoon
description: Constable painted this view of Flatford Mill in 1821; it was snubbed in London before winning a gold medal in Paris. It hangs in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A heavy, solid Madonna from a lost Pisa altarpiece
description: The central panel of an altarpiece Masaccio painted for a Pisa church in 1426, later broken up and scattered across Europe. It hangs in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A barmaid stares out while the mirror behind her misbehaves
description: Manet’s last major painting, from 1882, sets a Paris music-hall barmaid before a mirror that does not quite add up. It is in the Courtauld Gallery at Somerset House on the Strand.

title: Gods and horsemen taken down from the Parthenon’s heights
description: Pediment figures, metopes and frieze slabs carved under Phidias in the 440s–430s BCE, removed by Lord Elgin’s agents around 1801. They fill a long gallery in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: A puzzle painting of desire, deceit and jealousy
description: Bronzino painted this cool, crowded allegory in Florence around 1545, probably as a gift from Cosimo de’ Medici to the French king. It hangs in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Van Eyck may be looking at himself in a red turban
description: Painted in 1433, the original frame carries Van Eyck’s motto, “As I can”, which is why many see a self-portrait. It hangs in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Two marble Romans found in a Kent villa’s cellar
description: Two second-century marble busts, probably ancestors of a villa’s owners, were found in a cellar room at Lullingstone in Kent in 1949. They are now in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: Parliament rebuilds itself in Gothic after a great fire
description: After fire destroyed the old palace in 1834, Charles Barry planned the new building and Augustus Pugin drew its Gothic detail, down to the clock tower. It is the seat of Parliament beside the Thames.

title: A scribe’s heart is weighed against a feather
description: A painted sheet from the Book of the Dead of Hunefer, a royal scribe around 1275 BCE, showing his judgement before Osiris. It is in the Egyptian galleries of the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: An Assyrian king stages a lion hunt for his palace walls
description: Carved reliefs from the palace of Ashurbanipal at Nineveh, around 645 BCE, show the king killing lions released from cages. They line a gallery in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: A young king kneels before the Virgin and a host of angels
description: A small folding altarpiece made around 1395–99 for Richard II, who kneels with his patron saints; the angels wear his white hart badge. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Toy-like knights charge in perfect perspective
description: One of three panels Uccello painted around 1438–40 of a Florentine victory over Siena; the others are in Florence and Paris. This one, with Niccolò da Tolentino leading the charge, is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: An empress dozes at a window and dreams of the true cross
description: Veronese painted the mother of Constantine asleep by a window, around 1570, as angels bring her a vision of the cross. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Mary Magdalene reaches out and Christ pulls back
description: An early Titian of around 1514, showing the risen Christ telling Mary not to touch him, with a Venetian landscape behind. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Hogarth follows an arranged marriage from contract to ruin
description: Six paintings from about 1743 that Hogarth turned into best-selling prints, mocking a match between a broke earl’s son and a merchant’s daughter. They hang in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A 16-year-old widow is painted for Henry VIII to inspect
description: Holbein painted the young Duchess of Milan in mourning dress in 1538 when Henry VIII was looking for a new wife; she did not marry him. The portrait is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Spilled milk from a goddess turns into the stars
description: Tintoretto’s painting of around 1575 shows Jupiter putting the baby Hercules to Juno’s breast, with milk spraying up into stars. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Cupid steals honey and gets stung by bees
description: Cranach’s painting of the 1520s shows Venus in a big hat beside Cupid holding a honeycomb, a lesson about pleasure and pain. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A Persian queen mother bows to the wrong man
description: Veronese’s wide 1565–67 painting shows Darius’s family kneeling before Alexander and his friend, in Venetian costume. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Young workers cool off by the Seine, factory chimneys behind
description: Seurat’s first big painting, rejected by the 1884 Salon, shows men and boys on a riverbank west of Paris. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A Bruges priest kneels among saints in a walled garden
description: Gerard David’s panel of around 1510, with the donor Richard de Visch van der Capelle and saints in a garden. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A god leaps from his chariot at first sight of Ariadne
description: Titian painted this for the Duke of Ferrara in 1520–23, with Bacchus’s noisy procession and cheetahs pulling his chariot. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A huge blue satin sleeve leans out of the frame
description: Titian’s portrait of around 1510, once thought to be the poet Ariosto, with the sitter turning over his shoulder. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A mother poses as Charity with three boys clinging to her
description: Reynolds’s 1773 portrait of Augusta Cockburn and her sons, borrowed from an old master idea of Charity. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A steam train rushes over a Thames bridge in the rain
description: Turner’s 1844 painting of the Great Western Railway crossing Maidenhead Bridge, with a small hare running ahead. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A kept woman rises from her lover’s lap, suddenly ashamed
description: Hunt’s 1853 painting of a young woman in a London villa, full of clues such as a cat with a bird. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: Two disciples jolt in surprise as a stranger blesses the bread
description: Caravaggio’s 1601 painting shows a young, beardless Christ revealed at supper, with a fruit basket balanced on the table edge. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Christ stands calm in a river under a white dove
description: Piero’s panel of the 1440s, made for a church in his home town of Sansepolcro, with a Tuscan landscape behind. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: Leonardo’s chalk drawing of two mothers and two children
description: A large drawing of the Virgin, Saint Anne and the infants Jesus and John, around 1500. It was bought for the nation in 1962 and was shot at in 1987. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A waitress balances beer glasses in a crowded Paris bar
description: Manet painted this scene of a café-concert in 1878–80, cut down from a larger canvas. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A small folding altarpiece made for private prayer
description: A gold-ground triptych by the Sienese painter Duccio, around 1315, with prophets in the side panels. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: An old pope sits tired and thoughtful in his chair
description: Raphael’s 1511 portrait of the pope who hired Michelangelo for the Sistine ceiling; the beard was a vow he took during his wars. It is in the National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.

title: A lonely woman stretches her back after hours at her embroidery
description: Millais’s 1851 painting is based on Tennyson’s poem about a woman waiting for a man who does not come. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: Young Jesus cuts his hand in Joseph’s workshop
description: Millais’s 1849–50 painting of the holy family as working people was savaged by Charles Dickens. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: Sheep wander loose on a sunny cliff edge
description: Hunt painted this 1852 view at Fairlight near Hastings, with intense colour and sunlight through the sheep’s ears. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: Eighteen young women walk down a curving stair with instruments
description: Burne-Jones’s 1880 painting, with no story at all, was meant to be like music. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: A bronze athlete struggles with a snake wrapped round him
description: Leighton’s 1877 bronze, the painter’s first full sculpture, launched the New Sculpture movement. It is in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: A young woman in a London attic thinks back over her life
description: Stanhope’s 1859 Pre-Raphaelite painting of a woman by a window on the Thames, with coins and flowers scattered at her feet. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art at Millbank.

title: A fairy queen fawns over a weaver with a donkey’s head
description: Fuseli’s dreamlike scene from Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream, painted around 1790. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: A teenage poet lies dead in his attic room
description: Wallis’s 1856 painting of Thomas Chatterton, who died at 17 in 1770; the model was the writer George Meredith. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: Two girls light paper lanterns in a garden at dusk
description: Sargent painted this in the Cotswold village of Broadway in 1885–86, working only a few minutes each evening as the light faded. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art at Millbank.

title: A nun pleads with her brother in his prison cell
description: Hunt’s scene from Shakespeare’s Measure for Measure, painted 1850–53, shows Claudio asking his sister to give up her honour to save him. It hangs in Tate Britain at Millbank.

title: An African king lays down his crown for a beggar girl
description: Burne-Jones’s 1884 painting of the legend of a king who fell in love with a poor girl, set in a dark, rich interior. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art at Millbank.

title: Bacon mourns his lover in three dark panels
description: Bacon painted this triptych after the death of George Dyer in Paris in 1971, the night before a big Bacon retrospective opened. It is in the Tate collection, shown at Tate Britain at Millbank.

title: Two nuns dig a grave in a convent garden at sunset
description: Millais’s 1858 painting of a nun digging in a convent graveyard while another watches, with an ominous cloud overhead. It hangs in Tate Britain, the gallery of British art on the Thames at Millbank.

title: A nude stands propped against a heap of studio rags
description: Freud’s large 1988–89 painting uses the pile of paint rags in his studio as a backdrop for the figure. It is in the Tate collection, shown at Tate Britain at Millbank.

title: Narcissus kneels by a pool and becomes a stone hand
description: Dalí’s 1937 painting, with a poem of his own, which he took with him to meet Sigmund Freud in London in 1938. It is in Tate Modern, the gallery in the former Bankside power station.

title: A young viceroy in shining armour and a lace collar
description: Van Dyck painted the Viceroy of Sicily in Palermo in 1624, shortly before he died of plague. It hangs in Dulwich Picture Gallery, England’s first public art gallery, in south London.

title: A plaster cupid stands among onions and tilting tables
description: Cézanne’s 1894 still life combines a studio cast with paintings leaning against the wall. It is in the Courtauld Gallery at Somerset House on the Strand.

title: A young girl leans on a stone sill and looks straight at us
description: Rembrandt’s 1645 painting, once said to have been put in a window to fool passers-by. It hangs in Dulwich Picture Gallery, England’s first public art gallery, in south London.

title: A Tahitian woman lies awake as a dark bird watches
description: Gauguin painted this in Tahiti in 1897, naming it after Edgar Allan Poe’s poem The Raven. It is in the Courtauld Gallery at Somerset House on the Strand.

title: Eve hands Adam the apple while animals look on
description: Cranach’s 1526 panel of the Fall, with Adam scratching his head and a stag in the Eden thicket. It is in the Courtauld Gallery at Somerset House on the Strand.

title: An empress and saints celebrate the return of holy images
description: A Byzantine icon from around 1400 marking the restoration of icon veneration in 843, after the Iconoclasm. It is in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: A Russian icon got its nickname from dark overpaint
description: A late 14th-century Russian icon of Saint George on horseback, named for the black paint that covered it before cleaning. It is in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: An archangel stands at the top of a stair in carved ivory
description: The largest Byzantine ivory panel known, from the early 500s, with an angel holding an orb and a staff. It is in the British Museum in Bloomsbury.

title: Patterned brick and tiles crowd a tiny Victorian site
description: Butterfield’s Gothic Revival church of 1850–59, built in red and black brick with a richly decorated interior and tall spire. It is on Margaret Street, a short walk north of Oxford Circus.

title: A royal family poses, and the painter quietly mocks them
description: Goya’s 1800 group portrait of the Spanish royal family, with the painter himself standing in the shadows at the left. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s royal picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: Paradise, pleasure and hell crowd a single folding altarpiece
description: Bosch’s triptych from around 1500, packed with naked figures, giant fruit and strange machines of punishment. Two art historians look at it panel by panel in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery.

title: Picasso answers the bombing of a Basque town in black and white
description: Picasso painted this huge canvas in 1937 for the Spanish pavilion at the Paris World’s Fair. It only came to Spain in 1981 and now hangs in the Museo Reina Sofía, Madrid’s modern art museum near Atocha station.

title: A firing squad faces a man in a white shirt with arms spread
description: Goya painted it in 1814 to recall the executions of Madrid citizens by French troops after the uprising of 2 May 1808. It is in the Prado, Madrid’s royal picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: Gabriel visits Mary while Adam and Eve are thrown out of Eden
description: Fra Angelico’s altarpiece of around 1425–26, made for a convent in Fiesole, with the Expulsion shown in the garden at left. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery.

title: Ten life-size mourners fill a shallow gilded box
description: Painted in the 1430s for a crossbowmen’s guild in Leuven, the panel shows Christ lowered from the cross while Mary collapses in the same pose. It is now in the Prado, Madrid’s royal picture gallery.

title: Velázquez’s enslaved assistant paints himself into the scene
description: Juan de Pareja worked in Velázquez’s studio, was freed in 1650 and became a painter in his own right. His 1661 canvas, with his self-portrait at the left, is in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery.

title: Executioners haul an apostle up by ropes to his death
description: Ribera’s 1639 painting of the apostle Philip being raised for crucifixion, with onlookers in the crowd. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: A 26-year-old Dürer dresses like a gentleman
description: Dürer painted himself in 1498 in fine gloves and a striped cap, a picture of the artist as a gentleman. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: The wine god crowns a group of grinning farmhands
description: Velázquez’s 1628–29 painting puts a pale Bacchus among sunburnt Spanish drinkers. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: Apostles mourn Mary in front of a window onto a lake
description: A small Mantegna panel from about 1462, made for the Gonzaga court at Mantua, with a view of the lakes outside. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: A wild-eyed titan eats his own child on a dining-room wall
description: One of the “black paintings” Goya painted on the walls of his house outside Madrid around 1820, later moved to canvas. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: Apollo brings bad news to a blacksmith god
description: Velázquez painted this in Rome in 1630, as Apollo tells Vulcan that his wife Venus is unfaithful. It hangs in the Prado, Madrid’s great picture gallery on the Paseo del Prado.

title: Navvies dig up a Hampstead street while the idle look on
description: Ford Madox Brown spent more than a decade on this crowded picture of Victorian society, finished in 1865. It is in Manchester Art Gallery on Mosley Street, near St Peter’s Square.

title: Libeskind builds a museum from the shards of a broken globe
place: Imperial War Museum North, Salford Quays
description: Daniel Libeskind designed the museum, opened in 2002, as three curved fragments of a shattered globe. It stands on the Manchester Ship Canal at Salford Quays, opposite the Lowry arts centre.

title: Braque turns a railway viaduct into early Cubist blocks
description: In 1908 Georges Braque painted the hillside village of L’Estaque, on the city’s northern shore, following Cézanne who had worked there before him. Two art historians look at how the viaduct and houses collapse into simple geometric volumes.

title: A Medici bride steps ashore escorted by sea gods
description: Marie de Medici landed at the old port in November 1600 on her way to marry Henri IV. Two decades later Rubens painted the arrival for her palace in Paris, adding Neptune and naked sea nymphs. Two art historians unpack the political flattery.

title: Hitler opens a temple for art and a show to mock the rest
description: Paul Troost designed the House of German Art for Hitler, opened in 1937. Nearby, the Degenerate Art exhibition ridiculed modern works seized from museums. The building on Prinzregentenstrasse is now the Haus der Kunst art museum.

title: Greek temple sculptures change style between front and back
description: The pediment figures from the Temple of Aphaia on Aegina show Greek sculpture shifting from Archaic to Classical within a few years. Ludwig I bought them in 1812; they are displayed in the Glyptothek museum on Königsplatz.

title: A sleeping satyr bought by a crown prince for his new museum
description: The Hellenistic marble Barberini Faun sprawls asleep, drunk and openly sensual. Crown Prince Ludwig acquired it from Rome’s Barberini family in the 1810s for the Glyptothek, the sculpture museum he built on Königsplatz.

title: A duke commissions an ancient battle that fills the whole sky
description: Duke William IV of Bavaria commissioned Albrecht Altdorfer’s 1529 painting of Alexander defeating Darius, with thousands of soldiers under a curving earth and sky. It is now in the Alte Pinakothek, the city’s old master museum.

title: Two painted panels Dürer gave to his own city
description: Dürer painted the Four Apostles in 1526 as a gift to Nuremberg, inscribed with warnings drawn from Luther’s Bible. Elector Maximilian I took the panels to Munich in 1627; they now hang in the Alte Pinakothek art museum.

title: Dürer paints himself to look like Christ
description: Albrecht Dürer’s 1500 self-portrait, frontal and fur-collared, presents the artist with a gravity once kept for images of Christ. It hangs in the Alte Pinakothek, the Wittelsbachs’ old master gallery in the Kunstareal museum district.

title: A million tiny stones show Alexander staring down a king
description: This floor mosaic of Alexander the Great routing the Persian king Darius was dug up in Pompeii’s House of the Faun in 1841 and moved to Naples two years later. It now fills a wall of the National Archaeological Museum.

title: A worn-out Hercules leans on his club after the last labour
description: A giant Roman marble copy of a lost bronze by Lysippos, found in Rome’s Baths of Caracalla in the 1540s. It passed from the Farnese family to the Bourbon kings, and so to the National Archaeological Museum in Naples.

title: The statue that set the rules for the ideal male body
description: Polykleitos’s bronze spear bearer, made around 450 BCE, was meant to embody perfect proportion. The best surviving copy, carved in marble, came out of a sports ground in Pompeii and stands in the National Archaeological Museum.

title: A Pompeian woman pauses with a stylus to her lips
description: A small round fresco found in a house in Pompeii, showing a woman holding wax tablets and a stylus. It is in the National Archaeological Museum of Naples, which holds most of the finds from the buried towns.

title: Caravaggio paints the scourging of Christ during his Naples exile
description: Caravaggio painted it in 1607 after fleeing Rome on a murder charge, for a chapel in San Domenico Maggiore. It now hangs in the Museo di Capodimonte, the former Bourbon palace on the hill above the city.

title: A mortal lover burns up at the sight of the god in his glory
description: One of Moreau’s last great paintings, finished in 1895 and crowded with jewel-like detail. It hangs in the Musée Gustave Moreau, the artist’s own house and studio on rue de La Rochefoucauld in the 9th arrondissement.

title: An iron tower built for a fair outlasts the critics who hated it
description: Eiffel’s company put up the 300-metre tower for the 1889 Exposition Universelle, meaning it to stand for only twenty years. It rises over the Champ de Mars on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: Cast-iron plant stems mark the way down to the Métro
description: Guimard designed the green Art Nouveau entrances for the Paris Métro from 1900. Dozens survive; Porte Dauphine keeps one of the two original glass-roofed pavilions, at the edge of the 16th arrondissement.

title: A Gothic cathedral on its island, seen before the fire
description: Begun in 1163, Notre-Dame was filmed here before the April 2019 fire that brought down its spire; it reopened in December 2024. It stands on the Île de la Cité in the Seine.

title: Picasso glues printed oilcloth to a canvas and frames it in rope
description: Made in 1912, it is often called the first collage in modern art. It is in the Musée national Picasso, housed in the Hôtel Salé, a 17th-century mansion in the Marais.

title: Monet sets up his easel inside a station full of steam
description: One of a dozen views Monet painted of the Saint-Lazare station in 1877. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, itself a converted railway station on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: Sunlight falls in patches on a dress in a Montmartre garden
description: Renoir painted this in 1876 in the overgrown garden of his rue Cortot studio, with dappled light scattered over the figures. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: Strollers and sailboats on the river at Argenteuil
description: Monet lived in Argenteuil, a short train ride from Paris, and painted this promenade by the Seine in 1872. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: A Sunday afternoon dance in a Montmartre garden
description: Renoir painted the crowd at the open-air dance hall by the Moulin de la Galette in 1876, many of them his friends. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: Morisot’s sister and nieces chase butterflies in a garden
description: Painted in 1874, the year Morisot showed at the first Impressionist exhibition, it shows her sister Edma and Edma’s daughters. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: Courbet paints himself at the centre of French society
description: A huge canvas from 1855 that Courbet called a “real allegory” of seven years of his life, with friends on one side and society on the other. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: A village funeral painted at the size of a history painting
description: Courbet painted the townspeople of Ornans, his home in eastern France, life-size in 1849–50, shocking critics used to heroes at that scale. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: A sister watches over a sleeping baby behind a veil
description: Morisot painted her sister Edma with her newborn daughter in 1872 and showed it at the first Impressionist exhibition. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: Ancient Romans sprawl at the end of an orgy
description: Couture’s huge 1847 Salon painting, a warning about moral decline aimed at his own time; the state bought it. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, Paris’s 19th-century art museum in a former railway station on the Left Bank.

title: Three shirtless workmen plane a Paris apartment floor
description: Caillebotte’s 1875 painting was turned down by the Salon as vulgar and shown instead with the Impressionists. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, the former railway station on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: A nude woman picnics with two dressed men and stares back
description: Rejected by the official Salon, Manet’s painting was the scandal of the 1863 Salon des Refusés. It is in the Musée d’Orsay on the Left Bank of the Seine.

title: Three poor women bend to pick up what the harvest left behind
description: Millet’s 1857 painting of gleaners, with a big harvest piled up in the distance. Critics saw it as a political picture. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, the former railway station on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: Teams of oxen drag ploughs through heavy autumn soil
description: Bonheur’s 1849 state commission, a large frieze of oxen made after close study of animals in the field. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, the former railway station on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: Two farm workers stop to pray as the church bell rings
description: Millet’s 1857–59 painting of a couple bowed over a potato field at dusk; later reproduced on countless plates and prints. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, the former railway station on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: Bathers picnic on a Riviera beach in dots of pure colour
description: Matisse’s 1904 painting of Saint-Tropez in Neo-Impressionist dabs, titled after a line by Baudelaire. It belongs to the national modern art collection and hangs in the Musée d’Orsay on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: Laughing dancers in stone shocked Paris operagoers
description: Carpeaux’s 1869 group for the façade of the Paris Opera was attacked as indecent and once splashed with ink. The original was moved indoors and is in the Musée d’Orsay; a copy stands on the Opera.

title: An aunt, an uncle and two cousins sit in a tense Florentine room
description: Degas painted his aunt’s family in Florence in the late 1850s, the husband turned away from his wife and daughters. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, the former railway station on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: Manet thanks a young writer who defended him in print
description: Manet’s 1868 portrait of Zola at his desk, with a print of Olympia and a Japanese woodblock pinned up behind. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, the former railway station on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: Three friends on a balcony look past each other
description: Manet’s 1868–69 painting includes the painter Berthe Morisot seated at the green railing. It hangs in the Musée d’Orsay, the former railway station on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: Sailboats rock beside a rebuilt bridge on the Seine
description: Monet painted the bridge at Argenteuil, the Seine town where he lived in the 1870s, with quick broken strokes on the water. This 1874 canvas hangs in the Musée d’Orsay on Paris’s Left Bank.

title: An orange rock hangs over a path in the Provençal woods
description: A Cézanne landscape from around 1895, from the collection of the dealer Paul Guillaume. It hangs in the Musée de l’Orangerie, the gallery in the Tuileries garden best known for Monet’s water lilies.

title: A Greek massacre painted as a raw news event
description: Delacroix showed this canvas at the 1824 Salon, two years after Ottoman troops killed and enslaved thousands on the Greek island of Chios. It hangs in the Louvre’s large-format French paintings galleries.

title: A reclining nude with a back too long to be real
description: Ingres painted this harem woman in 1814 for Napoleon’s sister Caroline. Critics complained she had extra vertebrae. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace that became France’s national museum.

title: Delacroix paints a women’s room he glimpsed in Algiers
description: Delacroix travelled to North Africa in 1832 and based this 1834 painting on sketches made in a house in Algiers. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace that became France’s national museum.

title: An Egyptian scribe with crystal eyes waits to take dictation
description: A painted limestone figure from Saqqara, made around 2600 BCE, with eyes of inlaid rock crystal. It is in the Egyptian galleries of the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: Napoleon touches a plague victim to win a propaganda war
description: Painted in 1804 to answer reports that Bonaparte had abandoned his sick soldiers in Palestine. It shows him calmly touching a sore. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace that became France’s national museum.

title: A folding ivory altar shows the Byzantine heavens
description: A tenth-century Byzantine ivory with Christ, Mary, John the Baptist and rows of saints, small enough for private prayer. It is in the Louvre’s objets d’art department, the former royal palace that became France’s national museum.

title: A winged goddess lands on a ship’s prow at the top of the stairs
description: A Hellenistic marble found in pieces on the Greek island of Samothrace in 1863, probably marking a naval victory. It stands at the head of the Daru staircase in the Louvre, the former royal palace.

title: A small Greek goddess with braided hair and a belted dress
description: A limestone figure of about 650–625 BCE in the early Greek Daedalic style, found in a store of the Auxerre museum in 1907. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: A queen’s silver Virgin plays with her baby
description: A gilded silver statuette that Queen Jeanne d’Évreux gave to the abbey of Saint-Denis in 1339, with a lily that once held a relic. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: A Sumerian ruler sits with his temple plan on his lap
description: Carved in hard black diorite around 2100 BCE, Gudea of Lagash holds a ground plan of the temple he built. It is in the Near Eastern galleries of the Louvre on the Right Bank.

title: A painter hugs her young daughter and shows a hint of teeth
description: Vigée Le Brun, painter to Marie Antoinette, showed this tender double portrait at the Salon of 1789. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: A Babylonian king’s laws carved into black stone
description: A basalt stele of about 1750 BCE topped by Hammurabi before the sun god, with nearly 300 laws below. Found at Susa in 1901, it is in the Near Eastern galleries of the Louvre.

title: Liberty climbs the barricades in the July Revolution
description: Delacroix painted it in 1830 after three days of street fighting toppled Charles X; Notre-Dame is visible in the smoke. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: Three brothers swear to fight for Rome as the women weep
description: David painted it in Rome and showed it at the Paris Salon in 1785, a severe Neoclassical scene a few years before the Revolution. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: A Byzantine emperor rides in triumph on five ivory plaques
description: A sixth-century ivory from Constantinople, probably showing Justinian, later owned by the Barberini family in Rome. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: A Mamluk brass basin later used to baptise French princes
description: Made in Egypt or Syria around 1320–40 and inlaid with silver and gold, the basin was used for royal baptisms in France. It is in the Islamic art galleries of the Louvre.

title: Shepherds find a tomb and read a warning about death
description: Poussin painted this second version around 1638, with shepherds tracing the words on a tomb in an ideal landscape. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: Apollo and Artemis shoot down Niobe’s children on a vase
description: An Athenian red-figure krater of about 460 BCE, found at Orvieto, with figures placed at different levels across the surface. It is in the Greek galleries of the Louvre on the Right Bank.

title: An English king poses off duty, still very much in charge
description: Van Dyck painted Charles I around 1635 in hunting dress beside his horse, relaxed yet commanding. It is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: Young Athenian women walk in procession on a Parthenon slab
description: A slab from the east frieze of the Parthenon, about 445–438 BCE, showing young women who wove Athena’s robe. It is one of the few frieze pieces in Paris, in the Greek galleries of the Louvre.

title: Henri IV falls for a portrait of his future queen
description: Part of the cycle of 24 canvases Rubens painted for Marie de’ Medici’s Luxembourg Palace in the 1620s. The whole series now fills the Galerie Médicis in the Louvre.

title: Winged bulls with five legs guarded an Assyrian king’s gates
description: Human-headed winged bulls from Sargon II’s palace at Khorsabad, carved around 713–706 BCE and dug up by Paul-Émile Botta in the 1840s. They stand in the Assyrian courtyard of the Louvre.

title: Mary holds her dead son against a plain gold sky
description: Painted around 1455 for a church near Avignon, probably by Enguerrand Quarton, with a kneeling donor at the left. It is in the French painting galleries of the Louvre.

title: Lovers linger before leaving the island of Venus
description: Watteau’s reception piece for the Royal Academy in 1717, which created the category of the fête galante. This version is in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: Soldiers ram a crown of thorns down onto Christ’s head
description: Titian painted this violent scene around 1542–43 for a church in Milan; it was taken to Paris by Napoleon’s armies. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on the Right Bank.

title: Two kneeling bulls once held up a Persian king’s roof
description: A colossal column capital of about 510 BCE from the apadana, or audience hall, of Darius I at Susa, in present-day Iran. It is in the Near Eastern galleries of the Louvre.

title: A woman holds King David’s letter and considers what it means
description: Rembrandt’s 1654 painting, probably modelled by his partner Hendrickje Stoffels, shows Bathsheba with the king’s summons in her hand. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: Ibex with sweeping horns painted on a 6,000-year-old pot
description: A thin painted beaker from a cemetery at Susa, about 4200–3500 BCE, its ibex reduced to a few bold shapes. It is in the Near Eastern galleries of the Louvre on the Right Bank.

title: A Roman father sits in shadow as his executed sons come home
description: David showed this painting in 1789, just as the Revolution began: Brutus had ordered his own sons’ deaths for treason. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: Mary lies dead with swollen feet under a red curtain
description: Caravaggio’s 1601–06 altarpiece was rejected by the Roman church that ordered it; Rubens advised the Duke of Mantua to buy it. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: A woman steps between two armies to stop the fighting
description: David began this large painting in prison after the Terror and showed it in 1799, charging an entry fee. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: Two marble captives strain and sleep in unfinished bonds
description: The Dying Slave and Rebellious Slave were carved around 1513–16 for the tomb of Pope Julius II, then given away. They are in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: Moonlight falls through the trees onto a sleeping shepherd
description: Girodet’s 1791 painting, made as a student in Rome, shows the goddess of the moon visiting Endymion as a beam of light. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: A seraph with six wings marks Francis with Christ’s wounds
description: A tall gold-ground altarpiece of around 1295–1300, signed by Giotto, made for San Francesco in Pisa. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: A doomed king watches calmly as his palace is destroyed
description: Delacroix’s 1827 painting of an Assyrian king ordering his treasures and women destroyed before his enemies arrive. It shocked the Salon. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: An Akkadian king climbs a mountain over his fallen enemies
description: A pink limestone stele from around 2250 BCE, carried off to Susa as war booty a thousand years later and found there by French archaeologists. It is in the Louvre’s Near Eastern antiquities galleries.

title: A poor family pose with bread and wine in a dark room
description: A 1640s painting by one of the Le Nain brothers, showing a rural household with unusual dignity. It hangs in the Louvre, the former royal palace on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: Mary, Jesus and John meet in a gentle meadow
description: Raphael painted this Madonna in 1507 in Florence, soon after studying Leonardo’s pyramid-shaped groups. It entered the French royal collection under Francis I and hangs in the Louvre on Paris’s Right Bank.

title: A wig-maker’s dummy fitted with a ruler, a wallet and a tape
description: Hausmann built this Dada head around 1920 from a hairdresser’s dummy and bits of measuring kit. It is in the Musée national d’art moderne at the Centre Pompidou in the Beaubourg area.

title: Transparent shapes overlap like coloured glass on black
description: A 1924 painting by the Hungarian artist who taught at the Bauhaus, testing how light and transparency can be painted. It is in the Musée National d’Art Moderne at the Centre Pompidou in Paris.

title: A Berlin writer sits alone with a cigarette and a monocle
description: Dix’s 1926 portrait of a journalist became a picture of the Weimar “new woman”. The museum bought it from Dix in 1961. It is in the Musée National d’Art Moderne at the Centre Pompidou in Paris.

title: An opera house built as a stage for the audience itself
description: Charles Garnier’s opera house, built 1861–75 under Napoleon III, with its grand staircase and gilded foyer. The Palais Garnier stands on the Place de l’Opéra at the end of the Avenue de l’Opéra.

title: An abbot fills a church with light and Gothic begins
description: Abbot Suger rebuilt the choir of the royal abbey of Saint-Denis in the 1140s with ribbed vaults and tall windows. The basilica, burial place of French kings, is in Saint-Denis on the northern edge of Paris.

title: A tiny church squeezes a whole dome onto a street corner
place: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane church
description: Borromini’s first church fits on a cramped crossroads plot about the size of one of St Peter’s piers. Its walls ripple in and out and its oval dome is coffered with crosses, octagons and hexagons that shrink as they rise toward the lantern.

title: A tax collector looks up as a beam of light picks him out
description: Caravaggio’s first big public commission still hangs where he painted it, in the Contarelli Chapel of San Luigi dei Francesi, the French national church. Christ points at a group of men counting money in a dim room, and one of them is about to be chosen.

title: A young sculptor carves David mid-throw, biting his lip
description: Bernini was in his mid-twenties when he carved this David for Cardinal Scipione Borghese. Unlike Michelangelo’s calm hero, his figure twists in the instant before the stone flies. It stands in the Galleria Borghese, the cardinal’s villa museum.

title: Two brothers cover a cardinal’s ceiling in pagan love stories
description: Annibale Carracci, helped by his brother Agostino, filled the gallery of Palazzo Farnese with the loves of the gods, painted as if they were framed pictures hung on the vault. The palace is now the French embassy and opens only for booked tours.

title: A saint swoons in a chapel staged like a theatre
place: Cornaro Chapel, Santa Maria della Vittoria
description: Bernini built the Cornaro Chapel as a complete stage set, with hidden windows lighting the marble saint and an angel holding an arrow. Cornaro family members watch from carved boxes on the walls of Santa Maria della Vittoria, a small church near Termini.

title: A small temple by the river guarded Rome’s busy port
description: This compact temple to Portunus, god of harbours, stood beside Rome’s river port and cattle market, the Forum Boarium. It survived largely intact because it was turned into a church, and it shows Romans pairing Greek columns with an Etruscan-style podium.

title: Raphael paints the great philosophers into a papal library
description: Plato and Aristotle stride through a vast vaulted hall surrounded by Greek thinkers, some given the faces of Raphael’s contemporaries. The fresco covers a wall of the Stanza della Segnatura, one of the Raphael Rooms in the Vatican Museums.

title: Zaha Hadid pours concrete ribbons into an old army barracks
description: MAXXI, Italy’s national museum of contemporary art and architecture, opened in 2010 in the Flaminio district. Its curving concrete galleries and black stairs overlap and cross each other, built on the site of a former military barracks.

title: A fifth-century church still has its original cypress doors
